title: In 52 monitoring networks, decadal community warming came from warm-affinity taxon gains (45% of spatial expectation), not cold-affinity losses, through shared time trends (1948-2025)
abstract: Question: community temperature indices (CTI) follow only a small part of their spatial temperature gradients in time. Is the missing part on the warm side (warm-affinity taxa do not arrive or increase) or on the cold side (cold-affinity taxa persist)? Data: 73 BioTIME 2.0 networks, the North American Breeding Bird Survey and the UK Butterfly Monitoring Scheme (75 networks, 8,493 sites, 183,522 site-years, 1948-2025), GHCN_CAMS air temperature and HadISST sea surface temperature. Method: cross-fitted species thermal indices; the spatial CTI slope and the temporal CTI change of each network split into warm-side gains and cold-side losses, with a neutral-band correction for common changes in detection or richness; slopes on site warming trends (slow) and anomalies (fast); random-effects pooling; a space-for-time logistic emulator and a species-shuffle null. Results: in the 52 networks with a positive spatial CTI slope, the warm side followed the warming trend at 0.45 (95% CI 0.16-0.80) of its spatial slope and the cold side at -0.04 (-0.25-0.19); difference 0.50 (0.07-0.98). Under full tracking the estimator gives 1.26 and 1.12. The warm-side slope was 3.4 null SDs above the shuffle null (p = 0.024, minimum); the cold side was inside the null. Neutral bands of 15-50% and abundance weights gave 0.37-0.45 and -0.08 to -0.01. Year-to-year anomalies moved both sides by only 2-4%. With site and year fixed effects the sides were 0.26 (-0.05-0.69) and 0.13 (-0.28-0.63): the warm-side gain is a network-wide time change that local warming rates do not predict. Birds (BBS) gained warm-affinity species fully (0.95) but cold-affinity species increased (-0.53); butterflies (UKBMS) lost cold-affinity species as the emulator expects and gained too few warm ones. Conclusion: the decadal gap is mainly absent losses of cold-affinity taxa (persistence, extinction debt), with an exception in butterflies. Limitations: slow slopes contain all time-correlated changes; the neutral-band correction assumes no net response near the mean STI; heterogeneous BioTIME methods; no observer control for BBS.
